measurement.method: Capture both runs for real, measure with System.Drawing, round the measured value, then add a margin. No threshold is estimated without a run.

contracts.description: Two independent runs with --rt-shadows off must produce exactly the same final image (meanAbsError 0). This proves the raster fallback is bit-stable across processes, not just within one process.

Enabling DXR shadows must change a visible but bounded fraction of the frame: changedPercent must stay inside the measured interval. A value near zero means the pass silently stopped contributing; a value far above the ceiling means the image broke rather than gained shadows.

Vertex fallback (--mesh-shaders off) vs the default mesh path, with DXR shadows off in both runs so only the geometry path differs. This is deliberately NOT identical: the mesh path is known to be darker (see docs/MESH-BINDLESS.md). The contract pins the measured divergence, so an unreviewed fix fails just as loudly as a regression.

Two independent runs with --mesh-shaders off must be exactly identical (meanAbsError 0). This covers what mesh-off-vs-vertex cannot: the vertex fallback itself is deterministic and does not depend on the mesh path.
The shadow-mask debug view must not be identical to the final frame. This proves --debug-view mask is actually plumbed into the composite output instead of being accepted and ignored.
